thread:
Alex: Heads-up: after yesterday's canary we see steady memory growth on long streaming sessions (tool loops + longchat). Looks like KV residency keeps creeping up over time.
Priya: Repro steps? which variant/seq len?
Alex: Repro on canary cluster beta-2, model x-xl.q8_0, avg seq ~12k over 2hr session. Heap + RSS climb ~200MB/hr.
Chen: Did we rule out refcount leaks on the shard side?
Dani: I ran pprof on the runtime heap while replaying a recorded longchat — allocation hotspots point at kv_page_pin and pagechain walk.
Maya: Can you paste the pprof top?
Dani: Paste: 
```
(pprof) top
Showing nodes accounting for 65MB, 45.12% of 144.1MB total
      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%
    14.20MB  9.86%  9.86%     14.20MB  9.86%  runtime.malloc
    10.50MB  7.29% 17.15%     27.80MB 19.29%  kv_cache.pin_page
     8.30MB  5.76% 22.91%     12.40MB  8.60%  pagechain_coalesce
```
Alex: Interesting — pin_page and coalesce are up. Could be eviction hysteresis delaying frees.
Priya: We have a batching heuristic that holds recent KV pages for a grace window to serve immediate re-reads; maybe the window is too long under long context workloads.
Chen: Also saw unusual fragmentation in the slab allocator: small page objects not being reused because sizes oscillate with tool-loop patterns.
Dani: I added detailed tracing, saw that for repeated toolchain calls the same prefix hits cause repeated pins without corresponding unpin until session end. Suspect missing unpin in streaming resume path.
Maya: Any diffs between compile-time kernel selection branches? Could a kernel change affect pin/unpin ordering due to different async scheduling?
Alex: Canary included a kernel chooser tweak to favor fused-attn on long sequences; that changed the scheduling batch boundaries. Might be related.
Priya: Good call — fused-attn changes mean longer micro-batches and different KV reuse timing. If we combine that with long grace window, pages stay resident longer.
Chen: Quick mitigation options: 1) shorten KV grace window for long sessions; 2) force periodic background sweep releasing idle pins; 3) fix missing unpin in resume path.
Dani: I tried 2) in a local run: background sweep every 30s trimmed residency by ~30% on replay, but increased CPU usage ~4%. Tradeoff notable but acceptable for now.
Alex: Can we target 1) as a deployable config flag first? Shorten per-session grace based on observed seq length.
Maya: I'm worried about quality regressions if we drop cache too aggressively for short bursts. Need a heuristic: if session hits >8k tokens in N minutes, switch to short grace.
Priya: Agree. Add adaptive policy: grace = min(default, f(seq_rate, recent_hits)). We'll implement feature flag.
Chen: Meanwhile Dani to open a small PR adding an assert for unpin hit-rate and a metric kv.unpin_mismatch_count.
Dani: Will do. PR will include pprof snapshot and reproduce script.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout beta-2 -> 40% completed, monitoring enabled.
Alex: Also add flamegraph for the canary path; curious if kernel chooser causes syscall ordering that delays unpin.
Dani: Uploaded flamegraph to the thread: https://internal.redwood/fg/3789512468 — shows batching windows aligning with pin spikes.
Maya: Nice. Let's plan: Dani implements metric + repro PR, Priya adds adaptive grace flag, Chen inspects slab reuse for fragmentation, Alex monitors canary. If mitigations reduce ramp to <20MB/hr, promote patch.
Priya: I'll draft config and add a unit test simulating long session token churn.
Alex: Thanks. If anyone finds fast repro that doesn't require 12k tokens, ping me — will pause canary. :warning:
Chen: One more note — check quantized model runtime path too; kv access patterns differ with 8-bit kernels.
Dani: Acknowledged. I'll include q8 path in replay matrix.
Maya: Great thread. :thumbsup:
Alex: Closing loop tomorrow morning with updated metrics.
